# Flowing Hair Dollar

The Flowing Hair dollar was the first dollar coin issued by the United
States federal government, struck in 1794 and 1795. The design, by
Robert Scot, shows Liberty with flowing hair on the obverse and a small
eagle within a wreath on the reverse.

The 1794 issue had a mintage of 1,758 pieces, of which perhaps 140
survive. The finest known example, certified SP-66, traces to the first
day of striking and is plausibly the first silver dollar the United
States ever produced.

The type was replaced by the Draped Bust design in late 1795.
